photo.title: hus, huvudbonad, dans, fotografi, photograph
photo.reason: This 1906 hand-colored postcard photograph documents named Pomo men in ceremonial dance costume and regalia at Upper Lake, California, performing a roundhouse fire-eating dance — a clear ethnographic record of Pomo ritual dress and practice.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white); photographic print
photo.reason: Real-photo postcard of five Native American men in feather headdresses and dance regalia performing in Lakeport, Lake County, California—the heart of Pomo territory—with named individuals and museum caveat "Pomo (?)" indicating likely but unconfirmed attribution to this specific people.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: The photograph documents a large collection of Pomo baskets, numbered and displayed on a table and hanging by string — a documentary museum photo of objects made by the Pomo, matching the claimed ethnicity.

household.name: basket
household.title: basket
household.reason: A circular coiled basket with a star/floral pattern and shell-disc/glass-bead decoration, a classic Pomo basketry form; the museum explicitly attributes it to Pomo makers.

household.name: bärställning
household.title: bärställning
household.reason: The image shows a fine twined and lattice-twined basketry cradle/carrier attached to a wooden frame — Pomo people are renowned for exactly this basketry weaving technique, matching the museum's own note praising Pomo basketry skill.

household.name: fat, Korgfat, plate
household.title: fat, Korgfat, plate
household.reason: A tightly coiled oval basketry plate/tray with dark geometric banding, consistent with Pomo coiled basketry, a craft for which the Pomo are well known.

household.name: kärl, skål, Korgskål
household.title: kärl, skål, Korgskål
household.reason: This is a finely coiled basketry bowl (korgskål) attributed to the Pomo, who are famous for exceptional coiled basketry; it is not ceramic despite the record's category, but basketry is a classic Pomo product.

household.name: smoking-pipe
household.title: smoking-pipe
household.reason: A simple wooden smoking pipe with integral stem and bowl, museum-attributed to Pomo manufacture, consistent with objects used by this California people.

household.name: spelpinnar, Pinnar
household.title: spelpinnar, Pinnar
household.reason: Six wooden game/gambling sticks with fire-branded decoration, originally catalogued as Navajo but corrected by a museum specialist to Pomo — a reattribution with independent expert evidence, not just a country label. Such incised/branded gaming sticks are a documented Pomo (California) craft item.

household.name: basket
household.title: basket
household.reason: A small coiled basket with dark zig-zag pattern and beads, consistent with Pomo coiled basketry, a craft this people is well known for. The museum record attributes it directly to the Pomo.

household.name: skål, Korgskål, kärl
household.title: skål, Korgskål, kärl
household.reason: The image shows a finely twined coiled basket bowl, a classic Pomo basketry form (labeled "Korgskål" = basket bowl); Pomo are famed for exactly this kind of woven basketry.

household.name: Korgskål, kärl, skål
household.title: Korgskål, kärl, skål
household.reason: A bottomless woven basket used for acorn-pounding ("korgskål utan botten. För ekollonkrossning"), a well-documented Pomo/Californian basketry tool; basketry is not "ceramic" as claimed but is a genuine Pomo craft form.

masks-ritual.name: huvudprydnad, head-dress
masks-ritual.title: huvudprydnad, head-dress
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a feathered headdress with a long hide streamer attached to a rosette of feathers — a worn ceremonial/dance headdress, plausibly Pomo featherwork (California basketry/feather regalia region), matching the museum's own identification as "Pomo."

arms.name: dagger
arms.title: dagger
arms.reason: A dagger with an elk-horn blade incised with a zigzag pattern, wrapped grip in fur and cordage — a documented Pomo weapon type attributed by the museum to Pomo makers.

garment.name: huvudprydnad, feather headdress
garment.title: huvudprydnad, feather headdress
garment.reason: This is a feather headdress/band with dark feather tips flanking a central band of quills or plant fiber, a type of regalia made by Pomo and other California peoples; museum record attributes it to Pomo (acquired via Nordenskiöld), consistent with a worn ceremonial headband.

instruments.name: rattle
instruments.title: rattle
instruments.reason: A feather-and-cocoon rattle on a wooden stick, used as dance/ritual equipment by the Pomo of Northern California, consistent with documented Pomo cocoon rattles.

jewelry.name: mynt
jewelry.title: mynt
jewelry.reason: The image shows a strand of white clamshell disc beads ("mynt av musselskal" = shell-disc money), a classic Pomo craft product used as currency and ornament in central California — clearly something this people made, though it is shell, not metal.

jewelry.name: mynt
jewelry.title: mynt
jewelry.reason: The image shows a strand of shell disc beads ("mynt av musselskal" = coin of shell), a traditional Pomo shell bead money/necklace, a craft the Pomo of California are well known for. This is not metalwork but a beadwork/jewelry item made of shell.
